subtitle: What featured snippets are, how Google picks them, the controls that keep text out, and the trade-offs of opting out.
outcomes: Recognise a featured snippet and where it appears
Use nosnippet, data-nosnippet and max-snippet correctly
Weigh the cost of opting out
intro: Sometimes Google answers a question with a box at the top of the results, quoting a piece of one page. That box is a featured snippet.
This course uses Google's featured snippets guide for site owners, its help page for searchers, its meta description guide, its robots meta tag specification and its page on AI features.
Advice beyond Google's words, such as how to write answers, is labelled practitioner judgement.

lessons.title: What a featured snippet is
objectives: Describe how a featured snippet differs from a normal result
Say where a click on one lands

beats.caption: Featured snippets are special boxes where the format of a regular search result is reversed, showing the descriptive snippet first.
The box shows a little piece of a website that helps answer your question.
You can find them at the top of the search results, and in the 'People also ask' section.
Usually there's only one box, but sometimes there can be more.
Clicking one takes the user directly to the section of the page that appeared in it.

blocks.text: Google describes featured snippets as special boxes where the format of a regular search result is reversed, showing the descriptive snippet first. A normal result leads with the page title and link; a featured snippet leads with the answer text.
Google's help page for searchers puts it simply: this box shows a little piece of a website that helps answer your question. The featured snippets come from websites that Google finds.
Google lists the places you can find featured snippets.

items.text: At the top of the search results.

blocks.text: Usually there's only one box, but sometimes there can be more.
Google says clicking a featured snippet takes the user directly to the section of the page that appeared in the featured snippet.
Hypothetical: a snippet quotes the 'How often to water' paragraph of a plant care guide. A click lands the reader on that paragraph, not at the top of the guide.

takeaways.text: A featured snippet shows the answer text first.
It quotes a piece of a website.
It can appear at the top or in People also ask.
A click lands on the quoted section.

exercise.title: Spot your snippets
steps: Search ten question-style queries your pages target.
Note which show a featured snippet, and whose page it quotes.
Open People also ask and note any of your pages there.
Click one of your snippets and check where it lands.
exercise.prompt_template: Here are ten queries and what I saw for each: [notes]. Google says featured snippets show the descriptive snippet first, appear at the top of results or in People also ask, and a click goes to the quoted section. Summarise where I appear, where competitors appear, and which pages to look at first.

reflection: Which of your pages answers a question in one clear paragraph?
Does the section a snippet would link to make sense on its own?
lessons.whats_next: Next, how Google decides which page to feature.

lessons.title: How Google picks one
objectives: Explain who decides a featured snippet
Explain the length rules Google gives

beats.caption: Google systems determine whether a page would make a good featured snippet for a user's search request.
Google picks them based on how well they answer your question and how helpful they are.
Can you mark your page as a featured snippet? Google's answer: You can't.
Google does not provide an exact minimum length required to appear as a featured snippet.
Featured snippets only appear if enough text can be shown to generate a useful one.

blocks.text: Google says its systems determine whether a page would make a good featured snippet for a user's search request. Its help page adds that Google picks them based on how well they answer your question and how helpful they are.
Asked how you can mark your page as a featured snippet, Google's answer is short: You can't.

blocks.label: Watch out
blocks.text: There's no featured snippet markup to add. A tool or plugin that promises one is selling something Google says doesn't exist.

Google does not provide an exact minimum length required to appear as a featured snippet. It does say featured snippets will only appear if enough text can be shown to generate a useful featured snippet.

sections.heading: Snippets are made from your page

blocks.text: Google's meta description guide says snippets are automatically created from page content, and are designed to preview the content that best relates to a user's specific search. So Google Search might show different snippets for different searches.
Practitioner judgement: since Google picks text that answers the question, put a clear, self-contained answer right under a heading that names the question.

takeaways.text: You can't mark a page as one.
Snippets come from page content and vary by search.

exercise.title: Tighten one answer
steps: Pick a page that targets a clear question.
Find the paragraph that answers it.
Make sure a heading names the question and the answer comes first.
Check the paragraph makes sense if quoted on its own.
exercise.prompt_template: Here is a section of my page: [paste]. Google says it picks featured snippets based on how well they answer the question and how helpful they are, and snippets are made from page content. Suggest a heading that names the question and a self-contained opening answer. Label this as practitioner judgement.

reflection: Have you been told to add markup for featured snippets?
Which answer on your site is buried under a long intro?
lessons.whats_next: Next, the controls that keep your text out of snippets.

lessons.title: Snippet controls
objectives: Tell nosnippet, data-nosnippet and max-snippet apart
Explain what a low max-snippet does and doesn't do
Know which controls also reach AI features

beats.caption: nosnippet: blocks all snippets, including featured snippets and regular snippets, for a page.
It applies to all forms of search results, including AI Overviews and AI Mode, and prevents use as direct input.
data-nosnippet: marked text won't appear in featured snippets or regular snippets.
max-snippet: the shorter the setting, the less likely a featured snippet. It doesn't guarantee they stop.
max-snippet:0 means no snippet is shown. Equivalent to nosnippet.

blocks.text: Google says there are two ways that you can opt out of featured snippets, and its robots meta tag spec describes the controls behind them. Here's what each one does.

items.text: Blocks all snippets, including featured snippets and regular snippets, from appearing for a page.
An HTML attribute for parts of a page. Text marked with it won't appear in featured snippets or regular snippets.
Sets a maximum number of characters for a textual snippet. In general, the shorter the setting, the less likely the page will appear as a featured snippet.

blocks.text: Google says using a low max-snippet setting doesn't guarantee that Google will stop showing featured snippets for your page. Only a setting of 0 means no snippet is to be shown, which is equivalent to nosnippet.

Google's spec says nosnippet applies to all forms of search results, including AI Overviews and AI Mode, and will also prevent the content from being used as a direct input for them. max-snippet will also limit how much of the content may be used as a direct input for AI Overviews and AI Mode.

blocks.label: Remember
blocks.text: A snippet control is never only about featured snippets. Check what else it switches off before adding it.

takeaways.text: nosnippet blocks all snippets for a page.
A low max-snippet doesn't guarantee they stop.

exercise.title: Map your snippet rules
steps: Crawl your site and export robots meta tags and X-Robots-Tag headers.
List every page or block with nosnippet, max-snippet or data-nosnippet.
Write down why each one is there, and remove any no one can explain.
exercise.prompt_template: Here is a list of snippet rules on my site: [paste]. Google says nosnippet blocks all snippets and AI input, data-nosnippet keeps marked text out, a low max-snippet makes featured snippets less likely without a guarantee, and max-snippet:0 equals nosnippet. Explain what each rule does and flag any that look accidental.

reflection: Was any snippet rule on your site added by a plugin, not a person?
Is there text you'd rather never see quoted out of context?
lessons.whats_next: Next, Google's policies for featured snippets and the cost of opting out.

lessons.title: Policies and trade-offs
objectives: Explain when Google removes a featured snippet
Pick the narrowest control for a goal
Weigh opting out against AI feature eligibility

beats.caption: If a featured snippet breaks the rules, Google takes it down.
One policy: contradicting consensus on public interest topics.
To be a supporting link in AI Overviews or AI Mode, a page must be eligible to show with a snippet.
nosnippet on a whole page blocks all snippets and AI input.
data-nosnippet on one paragraph keeps only that text out.

blocks.text: Google's help page says that if a featured snippet breaks the rules, Google takes it down. One of the policies it lists is contradicting consensus on public interest topics.
Searchers can also give feedback. Google says that if you give feedback, it can learn to find even better answers.

Google says a page must be indexed and eligible to be shown in Google Search with a snippet to be a supporting link in AI Overviews or AI Mode. nosnippet blocks all snippets and prevents use as direct input for those features, and max-snippet:0 is equivalent to it.

Hypothetical: a law firm wants one disclaimer kept out of snippets. nosnippet on the page would cost it snippets and AI input everywhere. data-nosnippet on the disclaimer keeps only that paragraph out.
Practitioner judgement: match the control to the goal, and use the narrowest one that works.

items.text: Use max-snippet, knowing a low value doesn't guarantee featured snippets stop.
Use nosnippet, accepting that it also blocks AI input.

takeaways.text: Google takes down snippets that break its rules.
AI supporting links need snippet eligibility.

exercise.title: Fix one opt-out
steps: Pick a page that has nosnippet or max-snippet:0.
Write down the exact text you want kept out of snippets.
Replace the page-wide rule with data-nosnippet on that text, if that meets the goal.
Re-check the page in Search Console after it's recrawled.
exercise.prompt_template: Here's a page with a page-wide snippet rule and the reason it was added: [paste]. Google says nosnippet blocks all snippets and AI input, max-snippet:0 equals nosnippet, and data-nosnippet keeps only marked text out. Suggest the narrowest control that still meets the goal, and what it would cost.

reflection: Which page-wide rule on your site could be a single data-nosnippet?
Do any of your answers go against expert consensus on a public topic?
lessons.whats_next: That's the last lesson. Next, the conclusion pulls the four lessons together.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.text: A featured snippet reverses a normal result, showing a piece of a page first, at the top or in People also ask, and a click lands on that section. Google's systems pick it based on how well it answers and how helpful it is; you can't mark a page as one, and there's no exact minimum length. nosnippet blocks all snippets and AI input, data-nosnippet keeps marked text out, and a low max-snippet only makes featured snippets less likely. Use the narrowest control that meets your goal.

quiz.title: Course quiz
quiz.intro: You've reached the final quiz for Featured snippets and direct answers. The questions revisit what featured snippets are, how Google picks them and the snippet controls.

multiple_choice_overrides.explanation: Correct: Google's featured snippets page says featured snippets are special boxes where the format of a regular search result is reversed.

options: B. True, it is one paragraph
multiple_choice_overrides.explanation: Correct: Google says it does not provide an exact minimum length required to appear as a featured snippet.
Correct: Google says clicking a featured snippet takes the user directly to the section of the page that appeared in the featured snippet.

options: A. Text marked data-nosnippet won't appear in featured snippets
B. FAQ schema is required for featured snippet eligibility
C. max-snippet 0 is equivalent to nosnippet on a page
D. Featured snippets appear only if enough text can be shown to be useful
multiple_choice_overrides.explanation: Correct: no source says FAQ schema is required, and asked whether you can mark a page as a featured snippet, Google answers 'You can't.' Supported: data-nosnippet text stays out (A), max-snippet 0 equals nosnippet (C), and featured snippets need enough text to be useful (D).

Correct: Google says text marked by the data-nosnippet attribute won't appear in featured snippets or regular snippets. Wrong: nosnippet and max-snippet work on the whole page's snippet, and noindex removes the page from results.

options: A. Add nosnippet to the whole page so that nothing at all is shown
B. Add noindex to the whole page so that it leaves the results
C. Wrap only the disclaimer paragraph in data-nosnippet
D. Set max-snippet to 0 for the page as a whole instead
multiple_choice_overrides.explanation: Correct: data-nosnippet keeps only the marked text out, so the rest of the page can still show a snippet and stay eligible as a supporting link. Wrong: nosnippet blocks all snippets and AI input, noindex removes the page, and max-snippet 0 is equivalent to nosnippet.
